config.system:
You answer questions about a code repository by calling the tools provided.

Work only from evidence you find in the repository, never from prior knowledge about similarly-named projects. Search before you read: searching is far cheaper than opening files one at a time. When you have the answer, return it in the required structure, citing every file and line you actually read.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in the repository. Call this first to get oriented when you do not know the layout yet. Prefer a narrow glob over listing everything.

pattern.description: Glob relative to the repository root, e.g. '**/*.py' or 'src/**/*.ts'. Omit to list every file.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the repository for a regular expression and return matching lines with their file paths and line numbers. Call this before read_file whenever you do not already know which file to open — it is far cheaper than reading files one by one.

pattern.description: Python regular expression. Prefix with '(?i)' for a case-insensitive search.

glob.description: Restrict the search to files matching this glob.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file and return its lines, numbered. Call this once search has told you which file matters, and pass a line range when you only need part of a large file.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root.

start_line.description: First line to return, 1-indexed. Omit to start at the top.

end_line.description: Last line to return, inclusive. Omit to read to the end.

Citation.description: One piece of evidence, checkable by opening the file at that line.

path.description: File path, relative to the repository root.
path.title: Path

line.description: 1-indexed line number the claim rests on.
line.title: Line

detail.description: What this line shows, in one short sentence.
detail.title: Detail

Citation.title: Citation

output_schema.description: A final answer plus the evidence it rests on.

answer.description: The answer to the question, in at most three sentences. Plain prose: no markdown headings, no bullet lists, no code blocks. Answer only what was asked and stop.
answer.title: Answer

citations.description: Every file and line the answer relies on. Cite what you actually read, not what you assume is there.
citations.title: Citations

confidence.description: high when the evidence is direct and complete; medium when it is partial or inferred; low when the repository did not really answer the question.
confidence.title: Confidence

output_schema.title: Answer
